This is a completely different approach, and you might think I am crazy - but hear me out. Consider whether it works for you - if it doesn't, no harm - you can go ahead with your current plans.

If at all possible, build for a live fence, not a dead one. A live fence lasts for years decades, and can be designed to be as impenetrable as a board fence, if not more. It can also provide you with more than just privacy and protection.

For immediate results, set posts in concrete footings every eight feet. Nail boards across it at whatever gap gives you sufficient privacy. These need to last maybe 3 to 5 years. If the code in your local city/county doesn't object, you could just use hog panels and privacy-cloth.

Densely plant a variety of trees, shrubs and vines along the fence. Trees every 8 feet, filled in with thorny shrubs and vines in between. Your selection depends on the local conditions - climate, soil, water and light - but wherever you live in the world, there should be plants that will do well. Bias your selection towards trees that produce edible fruit and/or sap. Shrubs and vines that produce berries, fruit, flowers and/or fix nitrogen in the soil.

Within a year, you will get some edible output from the shrubs and vines - and it will get better each year. In about 5 years, most of your trees will be producing some output - and a thicket of thorny shrubs that no one will want to break through. You get flowers, food, shade, privacy, sound-absorption, air quality, wind-break, and more.

The downside is that in the first few years, you will have to help train the trees - maybe twice a year, cut back the branches that are growing the wrong way, chop-and-drop them on the ground. Occasional pruning of the bushes, if you really care. The maintenance is minimal, really - because this is the sort of thing that will tolerate neglect unless you are really particular about controlling the details. After maybe 3 years, it should be mostly on auto-pilot.
